siva: Heads up — dedicated canary for 2026-03-18 (merge M-4123) is showing a regression. p95 on short-seq workload jumped ~2.1x vs baseline after the merge. Customers on reserved pools could hit SLA risk if this reaches prod.

maria: rough numbers? CI perf or real canary traces?

siva: quick summary: perf-ci flagged a p95 increase in canary cluster 3. Local profiling shows an extra scheduler hop and kernel selector flip on ~45% of requests. Snapshot of profiler lines: 

```
# perf summary (short-seq load)
kernel_selector: chosen=kernel_v2_sparse for 47% requests (was kernel_v1_dense)
avg_batch_size: 3.1 -> 1.9
p95_token_latency: 120ms -> 255ms
scheduler: extra context switch at scheduler->merge_hop
```

jake: that kernel_v2_sparse is the one introduced in M-4123 right? I think the selector change used the new `batch_age` heuristic.

maria: yep. PR comment: "prefer sparse kernels for memory efficiency if batch_age > 5ms" — maybe batch_age calc is wrong under dedicated queuing.

olivia: can you paste the selector snippet?

siva: snippet from rollout build: 

```
if (seq_len <= 64 && batch_age > 5) {
  return kernel_v2_sparse;
} else if (avg_batch_size > 4) {
  return kernel_v1_dense;
} else {
  return kernel_v1_dense; // fallback
}
```

siva: under our dedicated canary burst pattern `batch_age` is being inflated by scheduling latency in the kernel routing layer (we saw ~7ms spikes), so lots of short-seq requests are being misrouted to v2_sparse which has worse per-token throughput at small batch sizes -> p95 climbs.

jake: confirmed with a quick repro on canary: forcing selector to always pick kernel_v1_dense drops p95 back to baseline.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for stack:redwood-runtime (reason: automated perf-slo check failed). See: https://ci.redwood/rollouts/2187654321

olivia: immediate action: hold rollout and revert the selector change in M-4123 (or patch selector to prefer v1_dense when avg_batch_size < 3). Which is faster?

maria: quick hotfix: change condition to check `avg_batch_size` before `batch_age` — low risk. I'll open a PR and tag for urgent review.

siva: open PR would be great. Also add a guard: if running in Dedicated mode, don't use batch_age until we stabilize the scheduler latency metric.

oncall: filing a rollback ticket now and pinging account execs for any affected Dedicated customers. ticket: https://issues.redwood/ISSUE-2231

jake: ran perf-ci with selector patched locally — CI job 2187654450 shows p95 restored on canary config. attaching diff in the thread: 

```
- if (seq_len <= 64 && batch_age > 5) {
+ if (seq_len <= 64 && (avg_batch_size >= 3 || batch_age > 8)) {
   return kernel_v2_sparse;
 }
```

olivia: that looks sensible and conservative. Approving hotfix now. :+1:

deploy-bot: PR #4278 merged to hotfix/selector-shortseq. Canary restart scheduled.

siva: after restart we should watch p50/p95 and also the `scheduler.hop_count` metric. I'll add a short eval run with short-seq synthetic load.

oncall: FYI sales notified. I'm keeping rollout on hold until we get two canary passes.

maria: ack. I'll follow up with a postmortem stub and link to the perf traces.

siva: thanks all. TL;DR: M-4123's batch_age-first logic causes kernel misrouting under Dedicated scheduler latency spikes -> p95 regression -> canary paused. Hotfix merged to prefer avg_batch_size guard; monitoring and two successful canary passes required before unhold. :thumbsup:
